conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a target of ~1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, leading to lower expected drawdowns. Returns will be modest, but the portfolio is better positioned for stability.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure while maintaining a small allocation.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.

balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing new, high-quality scanner setups. Expect moderate drawdowns with a focus on sustainable growth.

plan: Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to SOXL, bringing it to 10%, leaning into leveraged semiconductor exposure.
Add to METU, bringing it to 5%, leaning into strong AI/Software exposure.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It utilizes and adds to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring scanner setups. This approach significantly increases both potential upside and drawdown risk, and leveraged ETFs are subject to daily decay and rebalancing. Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage potential rapid losses.

plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, MUU, and METU to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETFs and high-beta single names.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.

income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month, aiming to park cash for yield. It significantly reduces leverage and high-beta exposure, favoring income-generating ETFs and broad index. While prioritizing low drawdown and reliable income, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
